headings.title: Licensure required to practice or hold out unless exempt

headings.title: Representing oneself as a psychologist and title proviso

headings.title: Definition of practice of psychology

headings.title: Application of psychological principles and methods
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: sets out a non-exhaustive list ('includes, but is not restricted to') of applications of psychological principles and methods.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections and L. 2025 merged-bill history note against archived source. Retained all draft titles, preserving permissive 'may' in subsection 1 and conditional highway patrol submission in subsection 2.

headings.title: Optional fingerprint requirement for psychologist applicants
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 1: permissive authority ('may require') for the state committee of psychologists to require fingerprints for licensed, provisional, and temporary psychologist applications.

headings.title: Fingerprint submission to highway patrol if required
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2: conditioned on the committee requiring fingerprints; requires submission to the Missouri state highway patrol for state and federal fingerprint-based criminal history background checks.

headings.title: Fingerprint routing, results, and committee access
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: governs central repository routing, fees, FBI forwarding under section 43.540, highway patrol notification, and committee access to discovered criminal history records notwithstanding section 610.120.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 9 subsections (including subdivisions (1)-(3) of subsection 7) and history note against archived source. Revised subsections 2 and 3 to reflect the section 337.029 exam-exempt/reciprocity alternatives.

headings.title: Application for psychologist license
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 1: covers temporary, provisional, and permanent license applications on committee forms, nonrefundable application fee, two-hour suicide training statement, and oath/affirmation under false-declaration penalties.

headings.title: Age, education, or exam-exempt evidence
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2: requires satisfactory evidence of age 21 and either section 337.021/337.025 education or qualification without examination under section 337.029; committee may require reasonable and proper evidence.

headings.title: Permanent license, examinations, and reciprocity exception
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: requires passing EPPP and committee-adopted exams for permanent licensure, except section 337.029 applicants who pass the jurisprudence and oral exams without retaking EPPP.

headings.title: Provisional license eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: authorizes provisional licensure for doctoral psychology graduates under section 337.025 meeting all requirements except licensing exams, oral exam, and postdegree supervised experience under section 337.025(2).

headings.title: Provisional license limits, termination, and renewal
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5: restricts provisional licensees to supervised services, lists automatic termination events (including section 337.035 discipline and 1-year expiration), allows renewal up to 2 years total, and requires rules for good-cause exceptions/variances.

headings.title: Temporary license for reciprocity or endorsement
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 6: requires immediate temporary license issuance to section 337.029 reciprocity or EPPP score endorsement applicants upon proof of out-of-state licensure, ABPP diplomate status, or National Register membership.

headings.title: Temporary license effect and end events
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 7 and subdivisions (1)-(3): grants full practice authority without additional fee until the earliest of permanent licensure, expiration of AHC appeal time after an ineligibility finding, or AHC ineligibility findings/conclusions.

headings.title: Examination schedule and subjects
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 8: mandates written and oral exams at least twice yearly for eligible applicants, specifies subject areas, and permits committee use of EPPP or other national exams in whole or part.

headings.title: Reexamination after failure
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 9: allows failing applicants to take a subsequent examination upon paying an additional nonrefundable reexamination fee.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections and history note against archived source. Revised subsections 1 through 5 to state the statutory 1989/1990/1996 cutoff dates, degree-and-experience scope, and pre-1990/pre-1996 eligibility limits.

headings.title: Doctoral or master's degree and experience evidence
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2 and subdivisions (1)-(2): requires satisfactory evidence of either a doctoral degree plus one year supervised experience or a master's degree plus three years experience, as defined by rule.

headings.title: Pre-1990 doctoral election between 337.021 and 337.025

headings.title: August 28, 1989 rules governing subsection 2

headings.title: Exam attempts for pre-1996 master's-level examinees
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5: applies notwithstanding section 337.025 or this section to subsection 2(2) master's-level applicants who took but did not pass the Missouri exam before August 28, 1996, granting equal attempts and time as doctoral applicants.

headings.title: Meaning of initial licensure

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections, nested criteria, history note, and original-rolls footnote against archived source. Revised subsections 1 and 6 for scope clarity; retained source footnote discrepancy ('includes*' vs. 'include' in S.B. 951, 2018 original rolls).

headings.title: Post-August 28, 1990 applicants governed by section

headings.title: Doctoral degree and supervised experience evidence

headings.title: Doctoral degree in psychology defined

headings.title: Supervised experience hour requirements

headings.title: Supervisor type by health service provider intent

headings.title: Postinternship and postdoctoral supervision conditions

headings.title: Rule for supervision exceptions

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections and history note against archived source. Revised subsection 3 to include EPPP score endorsement licensees alongside reciprocity licensees; noted source text's repeated word 'score' in subsection 3.

headings.title: Reciprocity license criteria

headings.title: Possible oral examination requirement

headings.title: Health service provider certification by reciprocity or endorsement

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 5 subsections and history note against archived source. headings.title: Replacement of lost, destroyed, or mutilated certificate

headings.title: Inactive license eligibility, renewal, and reactivation
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5: authorizes inactive licenses only for prior Missouri licensees no longer regularly practicing or holding out, exempts them from CE, keeps other chapter provisions applicable, and sets renewal and reactivation requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections and history note against archived source. Revised subsections 2 through 5 to reflect the non-certified practice proviso, health service provider scope, and 1989 exam-approved candidates.

headings.title: Practice limited to areas of competence

headings.title: Relevant education for health service provider certification

headings.title: Graduate program criteria for provider certification
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4 and subdivisions (1)-(3): requires degree or respecialization certificate from a recognized graduate program in APA-designated health service delivery areas meeting accreditation, designation, or institutional-labeling criteria.

headings.title: Deemed certification for 1989 licensees and examinees
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5: deems persons lawfully licensed on August 28, 1989, or approved to sit for examination before that date and later passing, to meet HSP certification requirements, still subject to subsection 1 practice limits.

headings.title: Automatic certification by credentials and fee
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 6 and subdivisions (1)-(2): grants automatic entitlement to HSP certification upon fee payment to lawfully licensed Missouri psychologists holding a health-service-delivery ABPP diplomate or National Register membership.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections (including all 15 disciplinary causes in subsection 2) and history note against archived source. headings.title: Discretionary complaints and grounds for discipline
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2 and subdivisions (1)-(15): committee 'may' file chapter 621 AHC complaints against current holders and persons who failed to renew or surrendered credentials for 15 causes, including section 324.012 offenses and committee 'Ethical Rules of Conduct' (subdivision (10) omits 'in' before 'this chapter').

headings.title: Chapter 621 hearings and permissive discipline limits

headings.title: Interested third party complaints and definition
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: permits interested third parties to file complaints, appear, or present evidence, defining the term to include a treated person's parent/guardian or financially responsible relative within the second degree.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 12 subsections (including subsection 12 subdivisions (1)-(5) and continuation paragraph) and history note against archived source. Minor refinements to subsections 3, 8, and 9 for phrasing, for-cause removal, and committee-vs-division rulemaking distinction.

headings.title: State Committee of Psychologists creation
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 1: creates the 8-member State Committee of Psychologists (7 licensed psychologists, 1 public member), abolishes the committee existing on August 28, 1989, and allows reappointment of current members.

headings.title: Appointment process and terms
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2: governor appoints on division director recommendation with senate advice and consent after nominee solicitation; sets 5-year terms, 10-year lifetime limit, and initial staggered terms.

headings.title: Member qualifications, diversity, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: sets residency, citizenship, 3-year licensure, practice diversity, initial master's-level appointment and full membership rights, domicile-removal vacancy, and unexpired-term appointments.

headings.title: Public member qualifications and role limits
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: sets citizenship, residency, voter registration, and conflict-of-interest qualifications for the public member and excludes the public member from technical licensure and competence determinations.

headings.title: Annual meeting, officers, and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5: mandates an annual meeting, election of chairperson and secretary, majority quorum, and secretary acting in chairperson's absence.

headings.title: Member compensation and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 6: authorizes division-set per-day compensation up to $50 plus reimbursement of necessary and actual expenses.

headings.title: Committee staff

headings.title: Governor's removal of members for cause

headings.title: Division rules and committee ethical rules

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 10: requires chapter 536 compliance (including section 536.028 if applicable) after August 28, 1998, repeals prior delegations while protecting pre-August 28, 1998 rules, and includes a nonseverability clause.

headings.title: Committee seal, suit, and certified records
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 11: authorizes committee to sue/be sued in its official name, requires a seal given judicial notice, and makes seal-certified copies admissible as evidence in courts of record.

headings.title: Renewal continuing education requirement
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 12, subdivisions (1)-(5), and continuation paragraph: requires 40 CE hours (at least 3 in professional ethics) in the 2 years before section 337.030 renewal, lists non-exclusive CE types, and directs committee credit-hour rulemaking.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections and history note against archived source. Revised subsections 4 and 5 to specify civil immunity and permissive attorney general injunction authority; confirmed subsection 7 'in addition to or in lieu of' wording.

headings.title: Violation as class A misdemeanor
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 1: makes violation of sections 337.010 to 337.090 a class A misdemeanor punishable as provided by law upon conviction.

headings.title: Refund of fees for violating services
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2: mandates refund of all fees or other compensation received for services rendered in violation of sections 337.010 to 337.090.

headings.title: Committee inquiry and enforcement duties
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: requires committee inquiry into violations and general enforcement of sections 337.010 to 337.090, and permits ('may institute') penalty actions.

headings.title: Good-faith reporting civil immunity
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: shields persons, organizations, associations, or corporations reporting or providing information to the committee or division in good faith from actions for civil damages.

headings.title: Permissive attorney general injunction requests
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5 and subdivisions (1)-(2): upon committee application, attorney general 'may' seek injunctions or restraining orders against unlicensed practice/offering or licensed practice posing a substantial probability of serious harm.

headings.title: Venue for enforcement actions
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 6: sets venue in the county where the conduct occurred or where the defendant resides.

headings.title: Actions in addition to or in lieu of penalties
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 7: actions under this section 'may be in addition to or in lieu of' other penalties under sections 337.010 to 337.090 and may be brought concurrently with other enforcement actions.

headings.title: Inmate, detainee, and chapter 552 complaint files

headings.title: Psychologist request to destroy older complaint records
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2 and subdivisions (1)-(3): upon psychologist's written request for pre-August 28, 1999 (DOC), 2008 (632.480-632.513), or 2021 (chapter 552) complaints without section 337.035(2) filings, requires record destruction, board/registry notification, and confirmation letter.

headings.title: No disclosure duty for unsubstantiated complaints
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: relieves subjects of unsubstantiated complaints under subsection 1 or 2 from disclosing them in subsequent psychology profession applications or representations.

headings.title: Fund transfer to general revenue limits
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2: notwithstanding section 33.080, bars transfer to general revenue until biennium-end balance exceeds 2x (or 3x if renewal is less frequent than yearly) prior fiscal year appropriation, lapsing only the excess.

headings.title: Transfer of funds from healing arts fund
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: directs division director to transfer psychologist committee funds from the committee of registration for the healing arts fund to the State Committee of Psychologists Fund.

headings.title: General purposes of the compact
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2 and purposes (1)-(6): states the six general compact purposes covering access, public/patient safety, state cooperation, information exchange, legal compliance, and mutual-recognition accountability.

headings.title: Social Work Licensure Compact citation

headings.title: Compact objectives

headings.title: Conditions for maintaining membership

headings.title: Designating eligible categories and optional issuance
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: eligible Member States must designate Multistate License categories; a Member State not meeting requirements for a category 'may choose, but is not obligated to' issue Multistate Licenses to applicants otherwise meeting section 337.1015.

headings.title: Optional Home State fee for Multistate License
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: permissive ('may charge') authority for a Home State to charge a fee for granting a Multistate License.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 8 subsections and history note against archived source. headings.title: General Multistate License eligibility

headings.title: Clinical category license requirements

headings.title: Bachelor's category license requirements

headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 7: if a Multistate License is encumbered, Multistate Authorization to Practice 'shall be deactivated' in all Remote States until no longer encumbered.

headings.title: Permissive deactivation when Remote State authorization encumbered
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 8: if a Multistate Authorization to Practice is encumbered in a Remote State, it 'may be deactivated' in that State until no longer encumbered.

headings.title: Joint investigations and shared materials

headings.title: Notice of Adverse Action to Data System

headings.title: Alternative Program in lieu of Adverse Action

headings.title: Executive Committee powers, membership, and meetings

headings.title: Commission finances and assessments

headings.title: Adoption at Commission meeting

headings.title: Notice of default

headings.title: Appeal by defaulting State

headings.title: Dispute resolution among states

headings.title: Legal enforcement actions
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 10(1)-(3): Commission may sue defaulting State by majority vote and Member State may sue Commission in D.C. or principal-office federal district for injunction/damages with fee-shifting; Commission remedies non-exclusive; only Member States may enforce Compact against Commission.

headings.title: Non-conflicting agreements with non-member states

headings.title: Amendment of the compact
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: Member States may amend the Compact; no amendment becomes effective and binding until enacted into law by all Member States.

headings.title: Liberal construction of compact and rulemaking

headings.title: Severability on constitutional holdings

headings.title: Enforcement of consistent state laws

headings.title: Agreements between Commission and states

headings.title: Home state definition
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 1: defines home state as a compact state where a psychologist is licensed to practice psychology.

headings.title: Multiple compact licenses and home state
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2: psychologist may hold multiple compact state licenses; if more than one, home state is where physically present when delivering services under interjurisdictional telepsychology authority.

headings.title: State licensure beyond telepsychology authority
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: compact state "may" require a psychologist not previously licensed in a compact state to hold a license for circumstances outside telepsychology authority.

headings.title: State licensure beyond temporary authorization
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: compact state "may" require a psychologist to hold a license for circumstances outside temporary authorization to practice.

headings.title: Conditions for telepsychology authority from home license
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5(1)-(5): home state license authorizes telepsychology in a receiving state only if the compact state meets 5 conditions, including active E.Passport, complaint mechanism, commission reporting, FBI/biometric identity history summary within 10 years of compact activation, and bylaws/rules compliance.

headings.title: Conditions for temporary authorization from home license
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 6(1)-(5): home state license grants temporary authorization in a distant state only if the compact state meets 5 parallel conditions, including active IPC.

entries.reviewSummary: Reviewed all 5 subsections and notes (L. 2018 H.B. 1719 merged with S.B. 660; effective 12-22-20 per § 337.170) for PSYPACT telepsychology privilege. Revised sub 5 to reflect that E.Passport revocation is triggered by restriction of either a license or receiving-state telepsychology authority.

headings.title: Recognition of interjurisdictional telepsychology privilege
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 1: compact states recognize the right of a psychologist licensed under section 337.110 to practice telepsychology in receiving states where unlicensed.

headings.title: Requirements to exercise telepsychology authority
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2(1)-(8): sets 8 eligibility requirements including accredited/equivalent graduate psychology degree, program criteria (a)-(j), full unrestricted home license, clean adverse-action and identity-history criminal record per commission rules, active E.Passport, attestations/release, and other commission criteria.

headings.title: Home state authority over license
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: home state maintains authority over the license of any psychologist practicing into a receiving state under telepsychology authority.

headings.title: Receiving state scope and action
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: psychologist is subject to receiving state's scope of practice; receiving state "may" limit or revoke telepsychology authority under due process and take necessary protective actions, and must promptly notify home state and commission.

headings.title: E.Passport revocation upon license or authority restriction
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5: restriction, suspension, or limitation of a license in any home/compact state or of telepsychology authority in any receiving state revokes the E.Passport and ends telepsychology eligibility. Revised title to include authority restriction.

entries.reviewSummary: Reviewed all 5 subsections and notes (L. 2018 H.B. 1719 merged with S.B. 660; effective 12-22-20 per § 337.170) for PSYPACT temporary authorization to practice. headings.title: Recognition of temporary practice authorization
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 1: compact states recognize the right of a psychologist licensed under section 337.110 to practice temporarily in distant states where unlicensed.

headings.title: Requirements for temporary authorization
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2(1)-(8): sets 8 temporary-authorization requirements including graduate degree, program criteria (a)-(j), unrestricted home license, no disqualifying adverse action or criminal record, active IPC, attestations/release on intended practice and work experience, and other criteria.

headings.title: Practice within distant state scope
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 3: psychologist under temporary authorization shall practice within the distant state's authorized scope of practice.

headings.title: Distant state authority and notice
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 4: psychologist is subject to distant state authority and law; distant state "may" limit or revoke temporary authorization under due process and take necessary protective actions, and must promptly notify home state and commission.

headings.title: IPC revocation upon license or authority restriction
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 5: restriction, suspension, or limitation of a license in any home/compact state or of temporary authorization in any distant state revokes the IPC and ends temporary-authorization eligibility. Revised title to include authority restriction.

entries.reviewSummary: Reviewed all 7 subsections and notes (L. 2018 H.B. 1719 merged with S.B. 660; effective 12-22-20 per § 337.170) for PSYPACT adverse actions. headings.title: Home and distant state adverse action powers

headings.title: Receiving state action and home state response
headings.reviewNote: Verified against subsection 2: receiving state "may" take adverse action on telepsychology authority within it; home state "may" take adverse action based on distant state adverse action regarding temporary in-person practice.

headings.title: No other remedies after subsection 3 action
